title: Kestrel Runner — launch spot
storyboard:
# Kestrel Runner — launch spot

Length 12 seconds at 30 fps. Deliver three cuts: 16:9 (1920x1080), 9:16 (1080x1920), 1:1 (1080x1080).

## Shot 1 (0:00–0:03) Product hero
- A teal running shoe with an orange sole slides in from the left over a dark night-city background.
- Caption reads exactly: Run the city

## Shot 2 (0:03–0:07) Detail
- Close-up of the orange sole, same teal and orange colourway as shot 1.
- The KESTREL wordmark is absent at 0:03 and fully visible by 0:05.
- A price tag reads exactly: €149

## Shot 3 (0:07–0:12) Call to action
- Headline reads exactly: Out 28 November
- A button labelled exactly: Get early access
- On the 9:16 cut, no text or button sits in the bottom 35% or the top 14% of the frame.
- On every cut, all text stays fully inside the frame.

versions.summary:
I've written `src/Video.tsx`: a 12-second spot at 30 fps (360 frames) with three shots, and one component lays itself out for 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1. I haven't rendered it or run Kane against it, so all the layout checks below are done by hand, not by running it.

**Shot 1 — Product hero (frames 0–90).** A teal shoe with an orange sole, drawn in SVG, springs in from the left over a night city. The skyline has two layers that drift at different speeds, plus lit windows, haze, a wet street with moving light streaks and a reflection of the shoe. Speed lines trail it until it lands, then it gently floats. The caption **"Run the city"** rises up from behind a mask under an orange rule.

**Shot 2 — Detail (frames 90–210).** An orange wipe cuts to a close-up of the sole: teal mesh upper, stitching, sculpted orange midsole and tread lugs. The camera slowly pushes in and pans while a highlight sweeps across. The **KESTREL** wordmark is invisible on the first frame of the shot (0:03), wipes in from frame 104 and is fully visible by frame 136 (about 0:04.5), before the 0:05 deadline. A hanging tag reading **€149** pops in and swings to rest.

**Shot 3 — Call to action (frames 210–360).** A teal w

I moved every piece of text on the 9:16 cut out of the bottom 35% of the frame, but I haven't rendered it, so the new positions are calculated, not measured. Kane re-checks on its own.

Kane's failure doesn't say which shot or frame was at fault. In my draft, two pieces of text sat in the bottom band before shot 3 even started, and that is the most likely cause:

- **Shot 1:** the "Run the city" caption sat at about 66% of the frame height. I moved it up to about 55–60% and raised the shoe to make room.
- **Shot 2:** the €149 price tag sat at 72%. It now sits at about 25–32%, between the KESTREL wordmark and the sole, and I moved the sole down a little.
- **Shot 3:** the headline and button now stay between 16% and 62% of the frame height (it was 15% to 64%). The button used to rise into place from slightly below. It now settles from slightly above, so it never dips into the bottom band while animating. The headline still rises into place from just below its final position. By my numbers it stays above the line, but I haven't checked that on a render.

All of these changes apply only to the 9:16 cut. The 16:9 and 1:1 layouts are unchanged.
